results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around The Jolly Balloon Man, Sewer-veillance Cam and Bloom Tender.
results.text:
I built and submitted **Jolly Balloon Combo**, a four-color (white, blue, red, green) Standard brew.

**The plan**
Play mana creatures early, then land The Jolly Balloon Man. Next to Starfield Vocalist, each Balloon copy of Glamermite has its "when this enters, untap a creature" trigger happen twice. One trigger untaps the Balloon Man and the other untaps Bloom Tender.
- Bloom Tender makes up to 4 mana (one for each color among your permanents) and the copy only costs {1}. So the loop never stops, and you end up with any number of hasty 1/1 fliers plus unlimited mana.
- If Shocking Sharpshooter is out, every token entering pings the opponent twice, so you win in your first main phase. Otherwise you attack with the fliers.
- The fastest kill is turn 4–5, because Vocalist's warp cost of {1}{U} lets you cast it the same turn you go off.

**Why the key cards**
- **The Jolly Balloon Man:** for {1} it makes a hasty, flying token copy of another creature you control. You can only use it at sorcery speed, so you combo in your main phase.
- **Bloom Tender:** it makes all the mana. Llanowar Elves also works in the loop, but it only breaks even on mana, so you still get unlimited fliers, just no extra mana.
- **Sewer-veillance Cam:** a 1-mana artifact with flash that untaps or taps a creature when it enters and again when it leaves. It isn't a creature, so it can't be the loop piece. Instead it gives extra untaps: an extra Balloon activation, an extra Bloom Tender tap, or tapping a blocker. Late in the game, pay {3}{U} and sacrifice it to draw two cards. Vocalist doubles its enter trigger too.
- **Starfield Vocalist (4) and Virtue of Knowledge (1):** both double any trigger caused by a permanent entering.
- **Glamermite (4) and Flash Thompson (2):** both untap a creature when they enter. Flash Thompson is legendary, so you can only keep one copy at a time. It still makes unlimited mana, and its other mode can tap a blocker. Glamermite copies stay around as fliers.
- **Formidable Speaker (4):** discard a card to find any creature, so it fills whichever combo piece is missing. Under Vocalist it finds two. A Balloon copy of it is also a {1} tutor.
- **Get Lost and Lightning Helix:** keep you alive against the fast decks.

**The mana**
I followed the Aang deck's land count (it averages 22.6 lands): 22 lands plus 8 mana creatures. The lands are 12 shock lands, 4 Starting Town, 5 Verges and a Forest. That gives 19 green sources, 12 blue, 11 red and 11 white, and check_deck passed with no warnings. Green is the priority so Elves can come down on turn 1. Bloom Tender then fixes the other colors.

**Sideboarding**
- **Prowess (27.9% of the field), Selesnya Offense and Landfall:** bring in 2 Lightning Helix, 2 Abrade and 2 Tectonic Hazard. Take out Virtue, the Flash Thompsons and 1–2 Cams.
- **4C Control, Dimir Excruciator and Lessons:** bring in 3 Disdainful Stroke and 2 Valorous Stance (makes Balloon Man indestructible for a turn). Take out Helix and some Get Lost.
- **Azorius Skies:** bring in 2 Pick Your Poison (makes them sacrifice a flier).
- **Reanimator and graveyard decks:** bring in 2 Rest in Peace. Note that it also exiles your own discards from Speaker.

**Label:** this is a brew. Only the mana layout is borrowed from Aang, which plays Cam, Bloom Tender, Vocalist and Speaker. The tools found no recent lists using Balloon Man or Glamermite.

**Honest odds and caveats**
- Without mulligans, the chance of drawing Balloon Man, a doubler, Glamermite or Flash Thompson, and a mana creature all naturally by turn 5 on the draw is only about 21%.
- Counting Speaker as a fill-in, the chance of Balloon Man plus a doubler plus an untapper or Speaker by turn 6 is about 38%. That count doesn't credit Speaker for finding Balloon Man or Vocalist, which it can, so the real number is higher.
- If you can't combo, the deck plays a weaker game of flash creatures and removal.
- The deck dies to removal pointed at the Balloon Man in response. Cheap blockers and Valorous Stance help, but it isn't tested in tournaments.

winLine.does: Mana creature already on the battlefield (Llanowar Elves also works, mana-neutral). With Balloon Man + Vocalist + Glamermite out it taps for W, U, R and G.
Main phase: pay {1}, tap: make a hasty, flying 1/1 token copy of Glamermite.
Cast for its warp cost {1}{U} that turn (or hard-cast earlier). Makes the token's enter trigger happen twice.

Each token copy's doubled trigger untaps The Jolly Balloon Man and untaps Bloom Tender. That's more mana than the {1} cost, so you can repeat as many times as you want and end with any number of hasty 1/1 fliers plus unlimited mana.
If it's out, each token entering triggers it (twice with Vocalist): unlimited damage with no combat needed. Otherwise attack with the pile of hasty fliers.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I built a Boros Dwarves equipment deck around your three cards and submitted it as a brew. Nobody has played these cards recently: Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful each show 0 lists in the last 90 days. So there was no proven list to copy. I took the land count and approach from Boros Aggro and built the creatures and equipment from scratch.

**The plan**
Play cheap Dwarves on turns 1–2, then put cheap equipment on them for free or nearly free and attack. Kíli and Dáin's Company keep finding more Dwarves and equipment so you don't run out of threats. The best start: turn 1 Mauler, turn 2 Kíli, then Hard-Won Jitte and Stormbeacon Blade on Mauler at no equip cost. That makes a 5-power double striker that hits for 10.

**Main deck (60)**
*Creatures (21)*
- 4 Dwarven Mauler
- 4 Kíli the Resourceful
- 4 Dáin's Company
- 3 Giott, King of the Dwarves
- 3 Thorin Oakenshield
- 2 Dáin Ironfoot
- 1 Fíli the Pathfinder

*Equipment (11)*
- 4 Hard-Won Jitte
- 3 Dwarven Mattock
- 2 Stormbeacon Blade
- 2 Dire Flail

*Removal (6)*
- 4 Burst Lightning
- 2 Lightning Helix

*Lands (22)*
- 4 Sacred Foundry
- 4 Inspiring Vantage
- 4 Sunbillow Verge
- 2 Sundown Pass
- 2 The Lonely Mountain
- 3 Mountain
- 3 Plains

**Why these cards**
- **Dwarven Mauler:** Equip costs that target it are {2} cheaper. Hard-Won Jitte (double strike) and Stormbeacon Blade (+3/+0) both have equip {2}, so they cost nothing to put on Mauler. Dwarven Mattock's {3} drops to {1}.
- **Kíli the Resourceful:** Draws a card when another Dwarf or Equipment enters (once per turn). With three artifacts and/or legendary permanents (Kíli counts as one), your first equip each turn costs {0}. Nearly every card here counts: equipment are artifacts, and Giott, Thorin, Dáin Ironfoot and Fíli are legendary.
- **Dáin's Company:** Looks at the top 4 cards for a Dwarf or Equipment, and has lifelink when you control another Dwarf. Natural odds of drawing Kíli by turn 3 are 48.8%, and Company's dig pushes that higher.
- **The supporting Dwarves:**
  - Giott has double strike and lets you discard a card to draw a card whenever a Dwarf or Equipment enters.
  - Thorin gives your artifacts and creatures ward {1} once you have three artifacts/legendaries.
  - Dáin Ironfoot comes with a free Axe and gives each equipped attacker double strike.
  - Fíli makes a 2/2 Dwarf token whenever a non-token Dwarf enters.
- **Dwarven Mattock:** Attaches itself to a Dwarf when it enters.
- **Odds:** You'll have a 1–2 mana Dwarf by turn 3 97% of the time, and a Dwarf plus an equipment 83.2% of the time.

**Mana**
22 lands, with 19 red sources and 17 white. The check tool's suggestion was 22.3, and Boros Aggro decks average 23.4. I went one lower because the average mana value is 1.84 and only three cards cost more than 2.
- I kept lands that enter tapped to a minimum: only 2 Sundown Pass.
- The Lonely Mountain is a Mountain, so it turns on Sunbillow Verge's red. It enters untapped once you have equipment out, and later turns spare mana into 2/2 Dwarves.

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Sear
- 2 Abrade
- 2 Ghost Vacuum
- 3 Dawn's Truce
- 2 Bofur, Reliable Guardian
- 2 Magebane Lizard
- 1 Lightning Helix

**How to sideboard**
- **Prowess (21.7% of the field):** Bring in Magebane Lizard, the third Lightning Helix and Bofur (lifelink). Take out Stormbeacon Blade and Fíli.
- **Lessons (15.5%) and 4C Control:** Bring in Dawn's Truce to protect your board from sweepers like Fire Magic, plus Magebane Lizard and Ghost Vacuum. Take out Lightning Helix and Burst Lightning.
- **Selesnya Offense, Landfall, Elementals:** Bring in Sear (4 damage) and Abrade, which can also destroy an artifact. Take out Dire Flail and Stormbeacon Blade.
- **Dimir Excruciator and Reanimator:** Bring in Ghost Vacuum and Dawn's Truce.

**What I couldn't check**
- How the deck actually does against this field: there are no results for these cards. The sideboard plans are my reasoning from the meta shares, not tested results.
- I assumed you wanted a fast aggro deck rather than a slower midrange version.

winLine.does: Turn 1 2/1 that equips Hard-Won Jitte, Stormbeacon Blade or Dwarven Mattock for {2} less (free for Jitte/Blade).
Turn 2: draws a card off the next Dwarf or Equipment entering; once storied (3 artifacts/legendaries), first equip each turn is free.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I built this as an Orzhov (white-black) sacrifice deck, often called Aristocrats. It's a brew: none of the three cards you named shows up in tournament results, with at most one list each in the last 90 days.

**The plan:** Play cheap creatures that leave something behind when they die. Feed them to Umbral Collar Zealot, which can sacrifice them at no cost, and turn each sacrifice into value with The Sackville-Bagginses, Syr Vondam and Vito. Around turn 5 the opponent is losing life on each sacrifice while your board keeps refilling. Most of the deck costs 2 or less (average mana value 1.89), so it can also just attack.

**Key cards**
- **Greedy Freebooter (4) and Infestation Sage (4):** your fodder. When Freebooter dies you scry 1 and get a Treasure. When Sage dies you get a 1/1 flying Insect. Treasures and Insects are both tokens, so each one counts twice against Sackville.
- **The Sackville-Bagginses (4):** when it enters, you can sacrifice a creature or artifact to draw a card and make a Treasure. After that, every token you sacrifice makes the opponent lose 1 life. That covers Treasures, Insects, Allies, Clues, and the Warriors Voice of Victory makes after sideboarding.
- **Sacrifice outlets:** Umbral Collar Zealot (4) is the main one; each sacrifice lets you surveil 1. Bartolomé del Presidio (2) is a second outlet that grows a +1/+1 counter with each sacrifice. Popular Egotist (2) drains 1 and gains you 1 every time you sacrifice anything.
- **Payoffs:**
  - **Syr Vondam (3):** grows and gains you 1 life whenever another of your creatures dies. If it dies with 4 or more power, you destroy a nonland permanent.
  - **Vito (3):** sacrifice three things in one turn and you gain 2 life, the opponent loses 2, and you get a 4/3 flier.
  - **Tolls of War (3):** makes a Clue, then a 1/1 Ally the first time you sacrifice something each of your turns.
- **Removal:** Requiting Hex (4) is the best fit. Its optional extra cost puts a -1/-1 counter on one of your creatures, which kills a Freebooter or Sage on purpose, and paying it also gains you 2 life. Get Lost (3) and Bitter Triumph (2) handle bigger threats.
- **Odds (no mulligans, on the play):** by turn 3 you see one of 12 sacrifice enablers (the three outlets plus Sackville) 88.7% of the time. You see a Freebooter or Sage 75.1% of the time, and both together 65.6%.

**Mana:** 22 lands, taken from the Orzhov Lifegain deck in recent results (72 lists, about 22 lands on average). The lands are 4 Godless Shrine, 4 Concealed Courtyard, 3 Shattered Sanctum, 2 Bleachbone Verge, 2 Starting Town, 5 Swamp, 1 Plains, plus 1 Midgar, City of Mako. Midgar is a land that can instead be cast as a spell that sacrifices a creature or artifact to draw two cards. That gives 23 black sources and 18 white. I leaned black because almost every card needs black, while white is only for the two-color cards and Get Lost. The deck check passed with no warnings.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Against Prowess (17.4% of the field), Selesnya Offense and Boros:** bring in 2 Seam Rip and 2 Deep-Cavern Bat. Take out Bitter Triumph (paying 3 life hurts here) and 1 Popular Egotist.
- **Against Landfall and Elementals:** bring in 2 Pyrrhic Strike to kill their 3+ mana creatures. Take out 1 Tolls of War and 1 Bartolomé.
- **Against 4C Control, Dimir Excruciator, Dimir Midrange and Lessons:** bring in 3 Duress and 2 Voice of Victory. Voice stops them casting spells on your turn, and its Warrior tokens get sacrificed at end of turn, which triggers Sackville. Take out removal (Requiting Hex and Get Lost) since they have few targets.
- **Against Reanimator and other graveyard decks:** bring in 2 Leyline of the Void and 2 Strategic Betrayal. Strategic Betrayal also answers creatures with hexproof or protection.

**What I couldn't verify:** Vito, Syr Vondam, Tolls of War, Bartolomé and Midgar have no recent tournament results, so how strong this is has never been tested in competition. Expect to adjust the counts after some games: Egotist vs. Bartolomé, and how many Tolls of War.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Gideon's Memorial, Solitary Cell and Ajani Unrelenting.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) planeswalker deck that makes lots of tokens. It's a **brew**: this shell doesn't show up in recent results, and each of your three cards appears in only 1–5 recent lists. The deck was accepted with no warnings.

**The plan**
- Turn 2: play Gideon's Memorial or Solitary Cell.
- From turn 3: play a planeswalker each turn, using Memorial's extra mana.
- Walkers make tokens, Memorial pumps them, and removal and Cell keep threats off your walkers.
- Ajani Unrelenting finishes the game. Its −3 deals 4 damage to every creature except your tokens, which wipes their board but not your token army. Next turn its +1 gives your team +1/+0 and haste to swing for lethal.

**Why these cards**
- **Gideon's Memorial (4):** Turns tokens into 2/1 vigilance attackers. It also taps for one mana of any color that can only cast planeswalkers, so a 4-mana Chandra comes down turn 3 and a 5-mana Elspeth turn 4. Late in the game you can discard it for 4 damage to an attacking or blocking creature.
- **Solitary Cell (4):** A 2-mana answer to any of their permanents (except lands) with mana value 3 or less. Its draw ability needs you to discard a legendary card, so I gave the deck 20 legendaries: 13 walkers, 4 Memorials and 3 Toby. Spare copies of a walker become new cards.
- **Ajani Unrelenting (3):** Every time you use any walker's loyalty ability, it makes a 2/2 Cadet token.
- **Elspeth, Storm Slayer (3):** The key partner. It doubles all your token-making, so with both out, each loyalty activation makes two Cadets. Its 0 ability gives your whole team +1/+1 counters and flying. Its −3 kills a creature with mana value 3 or more.
- **Ajani, Outland Chaperone (4):** Makes a token every turn and kills tapped attackers.
- **Other support:**
  - **Chandra, Torch of Defiance (2) and Quintorius Kand (1):** extra planeswalkers.
  - **Toby (3):** makes a 4/4 token, and gives your tokens flying once you have four.
  - **Caretaker's Talent (2):** draws a card each turn you make tokens.
- **Removal:** 4 Burst Lightning, 3 Get Lost, 2 Lightning Helix and 1 Stroke of Midnight, to protect your walkers early.

**Watch out:** Ajani Unrelenting's −3 also kills your own Toby. Only cast it when you're fine losing him (the 4/4 Beast token survives).

**The mana**
- 24 lands, matching the 23.9 average of Boros Dragons lists. I borrowed that deck's lands.
- 21 white sources and 20 red, for Ajani's {1}{W}{W} on turn 3 and Ajani Unrelenting's {4}{R}{R}.
- Sunbillow Verge needs a Mountain or Plains to make red. The 4 Sacred Foundry, 2 Elegant Parlor and 7 basics turn it on.
- The deck checker flagged "no blue, black or green sources." That's only because Boros Dragons plays Multiversal Passage, so you can ignore it.

**Honest odds**
- You see Memorial or Cell by turn 2 about 71% of the time.
- You have Ajani Unrelenting by turn 6 about 50% of the time (Elspeth is the same). You have both only 23% of the time.
- So the full combo is a strong late game, not something you can count on. Most games you'll win with steady tokens from walkers.

**Sideboarding**
- **Jund Sacrifice (15%) and Reanimator:** bring in 2 Rest in Peace and the Stroke of Midnight. Take out Lightning Helix and Caretaker's Talent.
- **Elementals, Prowess and other fast decks:** bring in 2 Pyroclasm and 3 Seam Rip. Take out Quintorius, Chandra and a Toby. (Pyroclasm also kills your 1/1 tokens, so cast it before you build a board.)
- **Landfall and Boros Dwarves:** Seam Rip and 2 Split Up.
- **Azorius, 4-Color and Dimir control/midrange:** 3 Voice of Victory (opponents can't cast spells during your turn) and 2 Boros Charm (indestructible against sweepers, or 4 damage to finish). Take out Burst Lightning and Get Lost.

**What I couldn't check:** None of these numbers come from real games, since nobody has played this exact deck. Toby, Stroke of Midnight and Caretaker's Talent have almost no recent results either. Every card was confirmed legal in Standard.

winLine.does: Turn 2: taps for a mana that can only cast planeswalkers, and gives creature tokens +1/+0 and vigilance.
Turn 3: +1 makes a 1/1 Kithkin token each turn, or -2 deals 4 damage to a tapped attacker.
Turn 4 with Memorial mana: doubles every token you make; +1 makes two Soldiers, 0 puts +1/+1 counters on your team and gives it flying.

Turn 5 or 6: each loyalty activation makes a Cadet (two with Elspeth out). -3 deals 4 to every creature except your tokens, so it's a one-sided sweeper; +1 gives your team +1/+0 and haste for the kill.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Jeskai Revelation, Inevitable Defeat and Tablet of Discovery.
results.text:
I submitted a four-color instant-speed control brew (blue, red, white, with a light black splash). Its core is your three cards: Tablet of Discovery, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.

**The plan**
You play a draw-go control game: cheap removal and counters on turns 2–3, Tablet on turn 3, then everything you cast is an instant. Tablet can tap for RR that only pays for instants and sorceries, which is exactly what this deck runs. That makes Inevitable Defeat castable on turn 4 and the 7-mana Jeskai Revelation castable at the opponent's end step from turn 5 or 6. Most of the win comes from piling up value and damage: drains, burn, Monk tokens, and Torrential Gearhulk recasting your big instant for free.

**Why the key cards**
- **Tablet of Discovery (4):** The RR only pays for instants and sorceries, so it works with almost the whole deck. When it enters, it mills a card that you may play that turn, so it also replaces itself. You still only have about a 49% chance to see one by turn 3 on the play, so the deck doesn't depend on it.
- **Inevitable Defeat (4):** It can't be countered, exiles any nonland permanent, and drains 3. That's good against UW Control's counterspells and against things like Greasefang's vehicles.
- **Jeskai Revelation (3):** One instant that bounces, deals 4, makes two prowess Monks, draws 2 and gains 4. Three copies, because seeing two early is a mulligan risk.
- **Torrential Gearhulk (2):** Flash 5/6 that recasts an instant from your graveyard for free. Getting a second Revelation or Defeat out of it is the payoff.
- **The shell, borrowed from UW Control:** No More Lies, Consult the Star Charts, Memory Deluge, Get Lost and The Wandering Emperor. Lightning Helix (4), Fiery Impulse (2) and Deafening Clarion (2) are there for Mono-Red Prowess and Izzet Prowess, which together are about 20% of the field.
- **Odds:** You have about a 60% chance to see Defeat by turn 6, and about a 50% chance for Revelation.

**The mana**
26 lands plus 4 Tablets. The check tool recommended 26.1 lands; average mana value is 3.26.
- **Sources:** 19 blue, 17 white, 16 red and 9 black.
- **Why black is light:** Only Inevitable Defeat needs black, so 9 sources is enough for a 4-drop you rarely cast before turn 4–5.
- **Triomes (9):** Raugrin ×4, Xander's Lounge ×2, Savai ×2, Raffine's Tower ×1. They fix colors and can cycle away late. The cost is a lot of tapped lands, so play them on turns 1 and 3, or on turns where you're holding up nothing.
- **Fabled Passage:** It only finds the single Island.

**Sideboarding**
- **Mono-Red / Izzet Prowess:** Bring in Temporary Lockdown ×2 and Beza. Take out Memory Deluge, Gearhulk and one Revelation.
- **Greasefang:** Bring in Rest in Peace ×2, Vanishing Verse ×2 and Temporary Lockdown. Take out Fiery Impulse, Deafening Clarion and one No More Lies.
- **Izzet Phoenix:** Bring in Rest in Peace ×2 and Mystical Dispute ×2. Take out Deafening Clarion and one Get Lost.
- **UW Control / Lessons:** Bring in Dovin's Veto ×2, Mystical Dispute ×2, Narset, Spell Pierce and Kolaghan's Command. Take out Clarion, Impulse, Helix ×2 and Get Lost.
- **Golgari Midrange:** Bring in Supreme Verdict and Vanishing Verse ×2. Take out Fiery Impulse ×2 and one No More Lies.

**What it is**
This is a **brew**, not a proven list. Jeskai Revelation and Inevitable Defeat show 0 lists in recent results. Tablet shows only 5, all in Lessons. The mana and interaction come from UW Control and the four-color Niv-Mizzet decks, and the check tool passed the deck with no warnings.

**Not verified**
- The win turn (I set it as turn 8) is my estimate, not a simulation.
- Gearhulk's UU needs could be awkward with this many tapped lands.
- I haven't tested how it does against the fast decks; you'd need to playtest that. If prowess beats you, Supreme Verdict or more Lockdowns would be the next changes to try.

winLine.does: Turn 2: kills an early threat and gains 3, keeping you alive against Prowess and Golgari
Turn 3: mills a card you may play this turn; from then on taps for RR toward instants
Turn 4 (3 lands + Tablet): uncounterable exile of their best permanent, 3-point drain
Turn 5 at the opponent's end step (5 lands + Tablet RR): bounce, 4 damage, two prowess Monks, draw 2, gain 4
Flash in at the end of their turn and recast Revelation or Defeat from the graveyard for free
Closes it out with Samurai tokens and Monks while burn and drains finish their life total

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Tolarian Terror, Bushwhack and Eddymurk Crab.
results.text:
I built you a Simic Terror Tempo brew. No proven list exists to copy: Tolarian Terror and Bushwhack show no recent Pioneer results, and Eddymurk Crab appears in just one Izzet Crab list.

**The plan**
You play about 27 one-mana instants and sorceries to fill your graveyard fast. That lets you cast 5/5s for two or three mana from turn 3. Then you protect them with cheap counterspells and use Bushwhack to make them fight. Your opponent faces two or three huge bodies before they've done much.

**Key cards**
- **Tolarian Terror (4)**: costs {6}{U}, 1 less for each instant and sorcery in your graveyard. It's a 5/5 with ward 2, so removal costs your opponent two extra mana.
- **Eddymurk Crab (4)**: has the same cost reduction, plus flash. When it enters, it taps up to two creatures. It enters tapped if it's not your turn, but the tap trigger still works. Use it to stop attackers on their turn, or tap their blockers on yours for a big swing.
- **Bushwhack (4)**: early it finds a basic land (Island or Forest) to fix your mana. Once a 5/5 is out, it becomes 1-mana removal by making your creature fight one of theirs.
- **More threats: Cryptic Serpent (2) and Haughty Djinn (2).** The Serpent is a 6/5 with the same cost reduction. The Djinn makes your instants and sorceries cost 1 less, and its power equals the number of them in your graveyard.
- **Card draw and graveyard fillers: Consider, Opt, Sleight of Hand and Otherworldly Gaze.** Consider and Gaze can also put extra spells straight into the graveyard.
- **Interaction:** Stubborn Denial is especially good here. It becomes a hard counter once you control a creature with 4 or more power, which your 5/5s are. Spell Pierce, Into the Flood Maw, Ram Through and Snakeskin Veil round it out.
- **How often it comes together:** with no mulligans, you have at least one of your 12 threats by turn 3 about 89% of the time.

**The mana (19 lands)**
- 4 Breeding Pool, 4 Botanical Sanctum, 4 Yavimaya Coast, 2 Willowrush Verge, 1 Barkchannel Pathway, 3 Island, 1 Forest.
- That's 18 blue sources and 16 green. Willowrush Verge only makes green if you control a Forest or Island, and Breeding Pool counts as both.
- I copied the land count from the Izzet Crab list, which ran 19. The deck checker suggested about 24, but it judges the 7-drops by their printed cost. In practice they cost 2–3, and the 1-mana spells smooth your land drops, so I kept 19 on purpose.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Greasefang (12.7% of the field):** bring in 2 Soul-Guide Lantern and 2 Pick Your Poison. Lantern exiles their graveyard and Pick Your Poison makes them sacrifice the vehicle. Take out Ram Through and a Spell Pierce.
- **Mono-Red Prowess and Izzet Prowess (18.7% combined):** bring in 3 Aether Gust. Cut Spell Pierce and Otherworldly Gaze. Your 5/5s already wall their creatures.
- **UW Control and Dimir:** bring in 2 Mystical Dispute, 2 Negate and 2 Tamiyo's Safekeeping. Cut Ram Through, Into the Flood Maw and a Bushwhack.
- **Golgari Midrange:** bring in 2 Essence Scatter, Tamiyo's Safekeeping, and Aether Gust against their green cards. Be aware that Unlicensed Hearse is very common in that deck (433 Golgari lists) and it exiles your graveyard.
- **Izzet Phoenix:** Lantern, Dispute and Negate.

**What I couldn't verify**
I couldn't test how the deck actually plays against these matchups, and there are no results for this exact build. Your biggest risk is graveyard hate: exiling your yard turns your 2-mana 5/5s back into 7-drops.
